# Post-Processing Kinematic (PPK) in Emlid Studio {#sec-emlid-studio-ppk}

::: {.callout-note}
### Purpose of this Chapter
This chapter walks step-by-step through configuring and executing a differential Post-Processed Kinematic (PPK) solution in **Emlid Studio** on Windows. You will learn how to pair raw observation logs from an **Emlid Reach RS2** receiver with the decompressed **IBGE RBMC** base station data, set accurate antenna height offsets, enter official geodetic coordinates, and evaluate the quality of your solution track.
:::

## Introduction to Emlid Studio

**Emlid Studio** is a free, cross-platform desktop application designed specifically for post-processing GNSS data. Beneath its modern graphical interface runs an optimized implementation of the open-source **RTKLIB** engine, tailored specifically to handle multi-frequency, multi-constellation logs.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    subgraph Data Inputs
        R[Rover Log: Emlid Reach RS2<br/>Raw .UBX or .obs]
        B[Base Log: IBGE RBMC<br/>Decompressed .yyO]
        N[Broadcast Navigation<br/>.nav / .yyN]
    end

    subgraph Emlid Studio Engine
        P[Kinematic / Static Processing<br/>Double-Differenced Carrier Phase Filter]
        C[Antenna Calibration & Offsets<br/>Reach RS2: 134 mm PCO]
        S[Base Position Override<br/>Official IBGE SIRGAS2000 Coordinates]
    end

    subgraph Solution Output
        SOL[Position Solution .pos<br/>Quality: Fix vs. Float vs. Single]
    end

    R --> P
    B --> P
    N --> P
    C --> P
    S --> P
    P --> SOL
```

### Downloading and Installing on Windows

1. Download the Windows installer (64-bit, Windows 10/11) from the official Emlid download page:  
   [https://emlid.com/emlid-studio/#download](https://emlid.com/emlid-studio/#download)
2. Run the installer `.exe` and follow the on-screen prompts.
3. Launch Emlid Studio from the Start Menu or Desktop shortcut.

---

## Kinematic vs. Static Workflows

In the top-left corner of the Emlid Studio window, click the workflow drop-down menu:

![Emlid Studio Workflow Selection Dropdown](assets/images/emlid_workflow_dropdown.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

There are two primary workflows depending on how your Reach RS2 was deployed in the field:

1. **Kinematic Processing:**
   - **When to use:** The Reach RS2 was moving (e.g., mounted on a backpack, drone, boat, vehicle, or handheld on a survey pole while walking).
   - **Output:** A continuous temporal trajectory of positions (one position per recording epoch, e.g., 1 Hz or 5 Hz).

2. **Static Processing:**
   - **When to use:** The Reach RS2 remained completely stationary on a tripod or bipod over a physical ground benchmark (from a few minutes to several hours) to establish a new permanent point.
   - **Output:** A single, averaged, high-precision geodetic coordinate set with formal standard deviations.

---

## Step-by-Step PPK Configuration (Kinematic Workflow)

### Step 1: Loading the Rover Observation File

1. In the **Rover** section, drag and drop the raw file from your Reach RS2 receiver.
   - Emlid Studio accepts raw u-blox binary logs (`.UBX`), RTCM3 logs, or standard RINEX observation files (`.obs`, `.26o`, `.rnx`).
   - *Automatic Conversion:* If you supply a `.UBX` file, Emlid Studio converts it to RINEX in the background automatically.
2. Click the **Edit** button next to the rover antenna parameters:

![Loading Rover Observation File and Setting Antenna Parameters](assets/images/emlid_rover_settings.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

3. Set the antenna properties:
   - **Antenna Type:** Select `Reach RS2` from the dropdown list.
   - **Antenna Height (m):** Enter the physical height of your survey pole (e.g., `2.000` m) measured from the ground mark to the **Antenna Reference Point (ARP)**.

::: {.callout-important}
### Reach RS2 Internal Antenna Height Geometry
When you select `Reach RS2` in the dropdown, Emlid Studio **automatically adds the internal 0.134 m (134 mm) Antenna Phase Center Offset (PCO)** to your entered pole height.
- If your physical survey rod is 2.000 m tall, enter **`2.000`**.
- **Do not** manually add 0.134 m yourself (e.g., entering `2.134`), or you will double-count the offset and your calculated elevation will be 13.4 cm too low!
:::

---

### Step 2: Loading the IBGE RBMC Base Observation File

1. In the **Base** section, drag and drop your decompressed IBGE RBMC observation file (e.g., `base0750.26o`).
2. Examine the base station position fields:

![Loading Base Observation File and Entering Known Geodetic Coordinates](assets/images/emlid_base_settings.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

3. **Override the Base Position:**
   By default, Emlid Studio selects **"RINEX Header Position"**. As noted in @sec-ibge-rbmc, this header position is only an approximate autonomous estimate.
   - Click the position dropdown and select **Manual coordinates** (or Cartesian coordinates).
   - Open the official IBGE **Relatório da Estação** (the station PDF downloaded in @sec-ibge-rbmc).
   - Enter the exact geodetic coordinates:
     - **Latitude ($\phi$):** e.g., `-03.10506828` (or degrees, minutes, seconds).
     - **Longitude ($\lambda$):** e.g., `-60.02305029`.
     - **Ellipsoidal Height ($h$):** e.g., `78.452` m.
   - **Base Antenna Height:** Enter `0.000` m (because the official IBGE published coordinates refer directly to the station ARP on the physical monument).

::: {.callout-caution}
### Never Process Against Uncorrected Header Coordinates
If you leave the base position on "RINEX Header Position", your relative baseline will be precise, but your absolute positions will be shifted in space by 2 to 5 meters! Always copy the official SIRGAS2000 coordinates from the IBGE station report.
:::

---

### Step 3: Loading the Navigation File

1. In the **Navigation** section, drag and drop the broadcast navigation file.
2. You can use either:
   - The broadcast navigation file downloaded from IBGE (`base0750.26n` / `base0750.26p`), or
   - The navigation file recorded by your Reach RS2 during the survey (`.nav` or `.26p`).
3. If your rover log is in `.UBX` format, Emlid Studio extracts the navigation file automatically during conversion.

---

### Step 4: Fine-Tuning Advanced Processing Settings

Click the **Gear Icon** (Settings) in the top-right corner to open the RTKLIB configuration dialog:

| Parameter | Recommended Setting | Scientific Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Positioning Mode** | `Kinematic` (or `Static`) | Matches your physical field motion. |
| **Elevation Mask** | `15 deg` | Rejects satellites lower than 15° above the horizon, eliminating severe tropospheric delay and ground multipath. |
| **SNR Mask** | `35 dB-Hz` | Discards weak satellite signals attenuated by forest canopy, heavy rain, or foliage. |
| **Satellites / Systems** | `GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou` | Utilizes all available constellations tracked by Reach RS2 to maximize geometry (low PDOP). |
| **Ambiguity Resolution** | `Fix and Hold` or `Continuous` | `Continuous` is conservative and robust against cycle slips in dense forest; `Fix and Hold` is aggressive for open sky. |
| **Solution Direction** | `Combined` | Runs the Kalman filter forward from start to end, then backward from end to start, smoothing out ambiguities. |

---

### Step 5: Processing and Quality Control

1. Click the blue **Process** button in the lower-right corner.
2. Monitor the progress bar as the forward and backward Kalman filters run:

![PPK Processing in Progress](assets/images/emlid_processing_progress.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

3. Once processing finishes, Emlid Studio displays the interactive track plot:

![Emlid Studio PPK Solution Plot](assets/images/emlid_solution_plot.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

---

## Evaluating the Solution: Fix vs. Float vs. Single

The interactive map colors each calculated epoch according to its mathematical quality:

```{mermaid}
pie title Epoch Solution Distribution (High Quality Survey Target)
    "Fix (1-2 cm Accuracy)" : 96
    "Float (20-80 cm Accuracy)" : 3
    "Single (2-5 m Accuracy)" : 1
```

1. **Green — Fixed Solution:**
   - The carrier-phase integer number of cycles between satellite and receiver has been unambiguously resolved.
   - **Accuracy:** Horizontal 1–2 cm, Vertical 2–3 cm.
   - **Usability:** Publishable, survey-grade ground truth.
2. **Yellow — Float Solution:**
   - The algorithm could not resolve the carrier-phase ambiguities to exact integers and maintains them as real (floating-point) numbers.
   - **Accuracy:** Horizontal 20–80 cm, Vertical 0.5–1.5 m.
   - **Usability:** Suitable for broad reconnaissance or rough GIS boundary mapping, but **unacceptable** for high-precision vertical datums or flood-pulse monitoring.
3. **Red — Single (Autonomous) Solution:**
   - No differential corrections were possible for this epoch (insufficient shared satellites between base and rover).
   - **Accuracy:** 2 to 5 meters.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Quality Metric: Fix Ratio
In scientific papers and technical reports, always report your **Fix Percentage** (e.g., "Post-processing in Emlid Studio achieved a 97.4% fixed integer ambiguity resolution across all 14,200 recorded epochs"). If your fix percentage is below 80%, examine your baseline distance, satellite elevation mask, or check whether dense canopy obstructed satellite line-of-sight.
:::

---

## Inspecting and Exporting Solution Files

Click the **Show Result Files** folder icon. Emlid Studio generates:

1. **`*_events.pos`:** Contains the precise coordinates corresponding to time-marks (e.g., camera shutter triggers or manual point saves in Emlid Flow).
2. **`*.pos`:** The complete trajectory file containing timestamp (UTC or GPS Time), Latitude, Longitude, Ellipsoidal Height ($h$), solution quality flag (`1 = Fix`, `2 = Float`, `5 = Single`), number of tracked satellites, and formal standard deviations ($\sigma_N, \sigma_E, \sigma_U$).
3. **`*.csv`:** Comma-separated table easily imported into R (`sf`, `terra`), Python (`pandas`, `geopandas`), or QGIS.
